title: Security handoff decision log and triage notes - 2026-08-04
body:
Meeting: Security engineering sync — vulnerability triage, secrets rotation, and threat-model decisions
Date: 2026-08-03 10:00–11:00 PT (notes captured by Maya Chen)
Attendees: Maya Chen (sec-eng), Ravi Gupta (infra), Leah Martinez (platform eng), Jonas Hsu (SRE), Priya Nair (product-security), optional: Samir Das (console)
Absentees: N/A

Objective: finalize short-term mitigations for the high-priority backlog items, agree on a secrets rotation timeline for Dedicated onboarding, and lock in the threat-modeling approach for the Private deployment control-plane changes.

1) Quick status / ground rules (5m)
- Today's focus: move three items to remediation (owner + ETA), avoid reclassing without justification, and record decisions in this document.
- Triage banding reminder: Critical (exploit observed/PoC), High (remote exploitability, high impact), Medium (local/complex), Low (info-only).

2) Vulnerability backlog highlights (25m)
A. JIRA-SEC-5187: GPU host kernel upgrade required for CVE-2026-2145 (container escape vector)
- Origin: internal fuzzing + upstream advisory.
- Current status: reproducible PoC in staging with certain nvidia driver combinations.
- Decision: Immediate canary rollout to Dedicated-qa (non-customer tenant) with kernel 5.17.2 + driver 535.54.03.
- Owner: Jonas Hsu. ETA: canary by 2026-08-06, full Dedicated pool patch by 2026-08-12 (outage window: rolling reboots, 2h per pool).
- Mitigations until patch: enforce strict seccomp profile, disable privileged flags in affected images, and add runtime monitor rule to kill suspicious containers.
- Notes: Leah to file infra change request and schedule capacity to absorb evicted workloads.

B. JIRA-SEC-5179: Credential exposure pattern in telemetry pipeline (partial secrets leakage in debug logs)
- Root cause: verbose debug path in legacy log shim that prints key IDs when message length < 512 bytes.
- Decision: hotfix to strip secrets from logs merged (PR #76), deploy to canary by 2026-08-04 EOD.
- Owner: Ravi Gupta (deploy), Maya Chen (verification).
- ETA: verification complete by 2026-08-05.
- Long term: replace shim with structured-logging library that enforces redaction rules (proposal in confluence link).

C. New: Unauthenticated metadata endpoint exposure found in edge router (internal report)
- Triage: Medium -> escalate to High due to potential information disclosure of internal service names.
- Decision: temporary ingress rule blocking /meta/*, create test that proactively checks for open metadata endpoints.
- Owner: Leah Martinez. ETA: block rule live 2026-08-04 16:00 PT.

3) Secrets rotation plan for Dedicated & Private onboarding (20m)
Context: Dedicated customers will be onboarded next quarter; Private customers require documented rotation that meets SOC2 and customer KMS controls. Current inventory: mix of KMS-managed secrets and legacy vaults with manual rotation.
Agreed phased approach:
- Phase 0 (now–2026-08-10): Inventory & short-lived mitigations
  - Complete inventory (owner: Priya Nair). Add automated scans to detect plaintext secrets in configs (scripts in github link).
  - Backstop: enforce application-level masking (no secrets in logs) and enforce least-privilege KMS access.
- Phase 1 (2026-08-11–2026-09-01): Automate rotation for service credentials
  - Use rotation-scheduler (existing infra tool) with terraform-managed IAM bindings.
  - Implement multi-step rollouts: generate new secret -> deploy to canary -> validate -> swap -> revoke old.
  - Owner: Ravi Gupta + infra-automation.
- Phase 2 (2026-09-02–2026-10-01): Private deployment & HSM support
  - Integrate HSM-backed keys for Private control plane. Define KMS/HSM interface shim.
  - Compliance doc draft (owner: Priya Nair) for customer attestations.

Hard deadlines: rotation scheduler must be ready for Dedicated onboarding dry-run by 2026-09-15.
Operational constraints & mitigations:
- Avoid live key revocation during high-traffic release windows (deploy windows to be coordinated with release-engineering).
- Add circuit-breaker that fails open gracefully to prevent mass outages on key failures.

4) Threat modeling — Private control plane change review (15m)
Scope: new control-plane API to allow customer-managed VPC peering and edge connectors.
Findings and decisions:
- Attack surface: increased lateral movement risk between customer VPC endpoints and control plane.
- Decision: require mutual TLS + signed JWT assertions for all peer setup requests. No plaintext tokens.
- Network micro-segmentation: enforce eBPF-based filters in control-plane hosts; deny-by-default for east-west traffic except explicit flows.
- Audit: all peering ops must write an immutable audit event to the central ledger (append-only).
- Modeling task: Leah & Maya to produce a DFD (data flow diagram) and threat list by 2026-08-10. Use the Confluence threat-modeling template.

5) Operational follow-ups and monitoring (10m)
- Detection improvements: add a telemetry alert when more than 3 distinct token errors occur for the same service in 5m (Jonas).
- Runbook updates: update the vuln triage runbook with the new triage banding and eviction playbook (Maya).
- Post-mortem cadence: for any remediation that causes >3% customer latency regression rollbacks, create a lightweight RCA within 5 working days.

6) Decisions and rationale (log)
- Kernel upgrade (CVE-2026-2145): chosen because exploit PoC exists and patch path tested in canary. Rolling reboots minimize blast radius. (Owner: Jonas)
- Log redaction hotfix: prioritized due to direct exfil risk; immediate merge and canary deploy. (Owner: Ravi)
- Mutual TLS + signed JWT for peering: chosen to reduce token sprawl and give cryptographic binding to requests. (Owner: Leah & Priya)

7) Action items (owners + ETA)
- Jonas Hsu: schedule kernel canary + runbook for pool reboots. ETA 2026-08-06.
- Ravi Gupta: deploy log-redaction hotfix to canary and verify. ETA 2026-08-05.
- Leah Martinez: apply ingress block for /meta/* and produce DFD for Private control plane. ETA 2026-08-04 (block) and 2026-08-10 (DFD).
- Priya Nair: complete secrets inventory and start SOC2 alignment doc draft. ETA 2026-08-10.
- Maya Chen: update triage runbook, publish decision log, and schedule follow-up meeting in two weeks. ETA 2026-08-07.

8) Risks & open questions
- Risk: rolling kernel reboots could temporarily reduce capacity below committed Dedicated SLAs. Mitigation: pre-authorize burst capacity and notify impacted customers. (Action: Leah)
- Open question: should we require customer-facing operators to use YubiKey-backed admin auth for peering ops? Priya to research viability and cost. Due 2026-08-12.

9) Next meeting
- Tentative: 2026-08-17 10:00 PT — focus on verification results, rotation scheduler progress, and any new critical findings.

Appendix: quick links and references
- Confluence threat-modeling template: confluence://sec/team/threat-modeling/template
- Deploy PR for redaction hotfix: github.com/redwood-inference/sec/rotation-scripts/pull/76
- Related JIRA: JIRA-SEC-5187, JIRA-SEC-5179

Notes to self (informal):
- We should consider adding a small canary pool in a separate AZ specifically for kernel patches — reduces customer impact.
- Track post-deploy telemetry for 72h with baseline CPU/mem/latency to catch regressions.
- Reminder: re-run fuzzing harness on updated drivers once kernel patch applied.

-- end of notes
